name: Pectin, dried (extracted from citrus peel)
source: Dried food-grade pectin: illustrative proximate (per kg) water 100 g, polygalacturonic-acid backbone 870 g, ash 30 g (commercial pectin retains some bound calcium/potassium from the citrus peel it was extracted from).
notes: The polysaccharide backbone is modelled by its real repeating-unit molecular formula, (C6H8O6)n (polygalacturonic acid; real pectin is partially methyl-esterified, a small further mass fraction this file folds into the same C:H:O bucket rather than modelling separately — a stated simplification). Extraction from orange-peel (origin/citrus.ts) uses a real cited yield (pectin is typically 20-30% of dried citrus peel mass) via splitByProfile against this profile and peel's own remaining-pomace profile.
